name: Blood Lotus Petal
description: A curled petal of a deep arterial red, thick and slightly warm to the touch. Ground, it is one of the chief ingredients of the Pavilion's pharmacopoeia; whole, it should not be held long — it wants to be used.

name: Crimson Cinnabar Pill
description: A small dull-red pellet that leaves a heat on the tongue and, afterwards, a taste of iron. Closes the meridians around a wound and forces the body to keep fighting. Azure Cloud apothecaries will not sell its like.

name: Scarlet Pavilion Token
description: A small lacquered medallion shaped like a half-open lotus. The bearer is known to the Pavilion — and to its assassins, who will step aside rather than cross one of their own.

name: Blood-Petal Mantle
description: A long sleeveless robe stitched from overlapping petal-shapes of oiled red leather. It does not quite lie flat; the mantle seems to stir very faintly between breaths, as though the petals themselves remember how to open.

name: Fragment of the Crimson Registry
description: A single page torn from a ledger bound in red leather. The writing is in a clear schoolmaster's hand: names, dates, and a neat column of prices. Some of the names have been crossed through; some have a small circle beside them. You do not want to think about what the circle means.

name: Apostate's Cipher Page
description: A sheet of rice paper folded seven times to fit inside a boot-lining. Four names are written in a cramped, left-leaning hand — two in black ink, two in red. The red are Azure Cloud elders. The margins are scored with the small crossed-circle marks that the Pavilion uses for a debt paid in more than stones.

name: Pond-Drinker Sash
description: A length of crimson silk heavy with old Pavilion seals — one for each elder the Pavilion has buried without a tomb. Worn at the hip by those who have retrieved, for Red Feather, something the sect could not retrieve for itself. The silk is dark from the pond; the pond, from the silk.

name: Willow-Step Ring
description: A pewter ring with a band so thin it must be worn high on the knuckle. The stone is no stone at all — only a smooth river-pebble polished by a lifetime of nervous turning. It was taken from a thief's hand while the thief no longer needed it.
